logical_component_title: Database Backup Workflow (Postgres to SQLite backup)

vulnerabilities.title: Exposed Database URL in logs
vulnerabilities.description: The backup script prints the full DATABASE_URL to stdout after loading environment variables (print(db_url)). This can reveal database credentials and connection details in logs or process listings.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Remove or redact prints of the DATABASE_URL. Use a secure logger with redaction. Do not expose credentials in logs or stdout.

vulnerabilities.title: Plaintext passwords copied into backups
vulnerabilities.description: The backup process copies the User.password field directly into the SQLite backup, resulting in plaintext passwords being stored on disk.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Do not copy password fields into backups or redact them. If backups must include authentication data, store it only as a salted hash or token, not in plaintext.

vulnerabilities.title: Backups stored in plaintext and in a predictable location
vulnerabilities.description: SQLite backup files are created under a backups directory with a timestamped name and stored in the project directory without encryption or strict access controls.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Encrypt backup files at rest and store them in a secure, access-controlled location. Use environment-based paths, rotate backups, and ensure backups are excluded from version control.

vulnerabilities.title: Memory exhaustion risk from loading entire tables into memory
vulnerabilities.description: The code uses .all() to fetch entire result sets (e.g., all_users = session.exec(select(User)).all()), which can exhaust memory for large datasets. This can lead to denial of service under heavy load.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Iterate results in a streaming fashion (e.g., using Result iteration or batching) instead of loading all rows at once. Consider per-batch commits to balance memory usage and transactional integrity.

vulnerabilities.title: Hard-coded backup restore path and potential path exposure
vulnerabilities.description: The restore function uses a hard-coded path to a SQLite backup file (sqlite_file_name = 'backups\\26-11-2025-at-10_37_09-AM-Backup.db'), which can lead to accidental disclosure or reuse across environments and reduces flexibility.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Parameterize the backup path or load from a secure configuration/environment variable. Avoid hard-coded paths; support environment-specific backups with proper access controls.

logical_component_title: Database Restore Workflow (SQLite backup to Postgres)

vulnerabilities.title: Restore operation uses per-record commits leading to data integrity risk and potential partial restoration
vulnerabilities.description: The restoration workflow commits after inserting each record, without wrapping the entire domain restoration in a transactional boundary. If a failure occurs mid-domain, the target Postgres database can end up with a partially restored/inconsistent state and potential duplicate or conflicting keys. There is no rollback strategy across the domain restoration steps.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Wrap domain restoration in a single transaction or in batch transactions per domain. Use a try/except with rollback on failure. Consider bulk upserts with proper conflict handling and migrate IDs in a controlled manner. Add integrity checks (row counts, foreign key consistency) before and after restoration.
vulnerabilities.snippet:
for user in all_users:
    with Session(engine) as remote_session:
        new_user = User(
            id=user.id,
            email=user.email,
            password=user.password,
            first_name=user.first_name,
            last_name=user.last_name,
            session_active=user.session_active,
            last_active=user.last_active,
            profile_photo=user.profile_photo,
            is_superuser=user.is_superuser,
            plan=user.plan,
            total_scans=user.total_scans,
        )
        remote_session.add(new_user)
        remote_session.commit()"

vulnerabilities.title: Hardcoded backup file path and insecure file permissions risk
vulnerabilities.description: The SQLite backup file path is hardcoded and read directly. If the backup file is stored in a world-readable or otherwise insecure location, sensitive domain data (including user information) could be exposed. The path is Windows-specific, reducing portability and increasing risk if moved to other environments.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Make the backup path configurable via environment variable or parameter. Enforce strict file permissions (e.g., permissions that restrict read/write to service account). Validate the path against a whitelist and ensure the file is stored in a secure location. Consider using a secure storage mechanism or encryption for backups.

vulnerabilities.title: PII logging exposure in restoration progress
vulnerabilities.description: The restore routine logs per-record restoration including user emails (Console().print("Restored user {email}")). This can expose sensitive user data in logs and stdout, which may be retained or exposed unintentionally.

owasp_top_10.SECURITY_LOGGING_AND_MONITORING_FAILURES: A09:2021 - Security Logging and Monitoring Failures

vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Redact or obfuscate PII in logs. Log only non-sensitive identifiers (e.g., user IDs). Implement RBAC for logging and rotate logs. Consider structured logging with redaction policies.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing validation of environment variables and potential crash if DATABASE_URL missing
vulnerabilities.description: The code directly accesses os.environ['DATABASE_URL'] without fallback or explicit error handling. If DATABASE_URL is not set, this will raise a KeyError and can crash the restore operation.

compliance_controls.ISO27001_A14_SYSTEM_ACQUISITION: ISO 27001 - A.14 System Acquisition, Development, and Maintenance

vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Validate environment variables at startup. Use os.environ.get('DATABASE_URL') with a clear, user-friendly error if missing. Provide a structured initialization error and fail fast with logs indicating the missing configuration.
vulnerabilities.snippet:
postgres_url = os.environ['DATABASE_URL']
# Recommended:
# postgres_url = os.environ.get('DATABASE_URL')
# if not postgres_url:
#     raise RuntimeError('DATABASE_URL environment variable not set')
